Concat of segments that carry AAC audio gives the master a video start_time of 0.021 s and a non-monotonic DTS at the first boundary; ffmpeg's default CFR decode then DUPLICATES a frame (933 real frames read as 934) and the boundary check fails everywhere. Fix: video-only segments, audio concatenated as PCM and muxed once with atrim; clipqc/cutqc decode with -fps_mode passthrough.

finding: ComfyUI dropped connection twice in one session (2026-08-23) while a job sat queued: once mid-render (job lost from history on restart, landed.py correctly reported LOST and render.py --requeue reproduced it from the row), once again within minutes of confirming it was back up. Matches the old vault's R-040 finding (restart takes the queue and history with it) but recurring this fast suggests instability beyond a one-off restart -- worth checking ComfyUI's own console/log for a crash loop before the next long render.

render.py's job 'refs' dict keys are ref_image SLOT NUMBERS (0..8), and slot N is ALWAYS <Picture N+1> in the prompt text -- slot 0 is <Picture 1> and, on mm_clip_v1, also doubles as GetImageSize's master ref (sets width/height). Authoring a job's refs dict in any order other than the prompt's own <Picture N> order silently swaps identities: a 2026-08-23 apricot_paper proof job put the LOCATION plate in slot 0 (=<Picture 1>, described in the prompt as the character Bram) and every character one slot off -- rendered as a flat character-lineup with no location and no scene, not a crash. Caught by looking at the filmstrip, not by any check. A job's refs dict should be authored by reading off <Picture N> from the prompt line itself, in order, every time.

CONFIRMED (Ronan's call, 2026-08-23): on mm_clip_v1, ref_image_0 is not just 'the master ref that sets size' -- it carries materially more compositional weight than ref_images 1-8. Four-reference apricot_paper test: with a character (Bram) as ref_image_0/<Picture 1> and the location plate at ref_image_3/<Picture 4>, the clip ignored the location entirely and rendered a flat character-sheet lineup on the sheets' own backdrop. Identical prompt content, only the SLOT assignment changed (location moved to ref_image_0/<Picture 1>, characters shifted to 1/2/3): the clip opened correctly on the gate scene, rain, lantern, doors, with all three characters composited into it and holding the beat's blocking. Rule for every multi-reference clip prompt from here: put the LOCATION (or whichever reference should set the scene) at ref_image_0/<Picture 1>, never a character.
fix: reorder refs so the location is ref_image_0/<Picture 1> in every multi-ref clip prompt
